name: Belmond Hotel Monasterio
insider_take: This former 16th-century monastery sits at 11,000 feet above sea level, where ancient Inca walls meet colonial Spanish architecture in the heart of the Sacred Valley.
whats_special: The hotel's chapel still hosts daily Catholic mass, and its central courtyard houses an oxygen-enriched environment to help guests acclimate to Cusco's extreme altitude. Original Inca stonework forms the foundation, while Spanish colonial additions create a stunning architectural timeline spanning five centuries.
pro_tip: Book a room facing the central courtyard to enjoy the hotel's unique oxygen system and avoid altitude sickness during your first night in Cusco.
dont_miss: The hotel's resident priest leads evening tours through the original monastery corridors, and the property's location puts you within a 3-minute walk of both the Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun) ruins and San Pedro Market, Cusco's most authentic local marketplace.
pros: Historic 16th-century monastery setting with authentic colonial architecture
Prime location in Cusco's historic center near main attractions
Oxygen-enriched rooms to help with high-altitude acclimatization
Exceptional luxury service and amenities from renowned Belmond brand
cons: High altitude location at 11,000+ feet may require acclimatization
